assumptions: The rate card supplied is a PLACEHOLDER: a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE. No real roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM, designer) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet, so this estimate is indicative only and should be revisited once the team is actually staffed with roles and rates.

With only 1 FTE (Team member) available at ~40 hrs/week, total backlog effort has been converted to hours using an industry-standard rule of thumb of ~6 hours of effort per story point for a solo generalist handling design, build, test and deploy end-to-end (no specialization possible with only one role).

Total backlog is 24 tasks summing to 192 story points; at 6 hrs/point that is 1,152 'ideal' engineering hours. Because a single generalist must also handle context-switching, integration, testing, deployment, and rework across 24 disparate tasks (auth, payments, migration, accessibility, i18n, admin tooling, etc.), a complexity/overhead multiplier of ~2.5x has been applied, giving ~2,880 hours total - roughly 18 months of full-time solo work for 1 FTE.
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; all figures are derived from story points and standard heuristics, not observed velocity, and carry corresponding uncertainty.

The single 'Team member' role is used for ALL work (planning, engineering, testing, deployment, migration, accessibility, security) since it is the only role staffed on the rate card - this is almost certainly insufficient for a project of this breadth (payments, RBAC, GDPR, legacy migration, i18n, accessibility, observability) and should be flagged to the client as a staffing risk.
Priority breakdown cost is allocated proportionally by story points within each priority band against the total labour cost.
Non-labour costs (Stripe sandbox, migration tooling, accessibility audit, CI/CD infra) are rough indicative placeholders since no vendor quotes were supplied.

1 FTE at 1,152-2,880 hours implies a project duration of roughly 12-18 months if pursued sequentially by a single person; if the client intends a faster delivery, additional FTEs/roles must be added to the rate card.
Scenario range (+/-20%) reflects uncertainty inherent in point-to-hour conversion and the unusually broad single-role staffing model, not proven variance from actuals.
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 192 story points across 24 tasks. This yields ~2,880 hours, costed at the single $75/hr rate = $216,000 as the most-likely case, with +/-20% scenario bands to reflect estimation uncertainty. Priority totals are apportioned by each priority band's share of total story points. Non-labour costs are small indicative placeholders for third-party tooling/audits since none were specified. The dominant risk called out is that a single generic role/FTE is very unlikely to be sufficient in practice for this scope; the client should assign real roles (e.g., Backend Dev, Frontend Dev, QA, DevOps, PM) with differentiated rates and headcounts before this estimate is treated as firm."]

reductions.description: Descope Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase — 39 points total, ~20% of backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes ~576 hours of the 2,880-hour estimate (39/192 points x 2,880 hrs x $75), deferring roughly $43,200 of spend to a future phase.

reductions.description: Defer Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) and Usage analytics/reporting (PW-19, already counted above if kept) until after initial launch since portal can launch single-currency first.
reductions.effect: Removes ~195 hours (13/192 x 2,880) of labour from the current estimate, to be picked up in a later release.

reductions.description: Reduce Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) scope by migrating only active accounts/invoices first (e.g. last 2 years) rather than the full 400k/2M record history in this phase.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly half of the migration effort (~10.5 of 21 points, ~157 hrs) by narrowing initial migration scope, deferring historical backfill to a follow-up project.

reductions.description: Replace bespoke Design system and component library (PW-2, 8 points) with an existing open-source Angular UI kit (e.g. Angular Material) instead of building one from scratch.
reductions.effect: Saves an estimated 120 hours of build effort by adopting rather than building a component library, though some customization time remains.

reductions.description: Staff the project with a proper multi-role team (e.g. 2 developers, 1 QA, 1 PM) instead of a single generalist FTE, which typically reduces total elapsed hours due to specialization and parallel work even if headcount cost rises.
reductions.effect: Not a direct dollar saving in this placeholder estimate, but flagged because the current single-FTE/single-role model likely inflates hours via the 2.5x overhead multiplier; proper role specialization could shrink that multiplier and total cost once real rates are set.
